deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Riemann's own mathematics. It is the second side (folio 26r) of a letter from Karl Hattendorff, signed 'K. Hattendorff'. Hattendorff edited Riemann's posthumous memoir 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Abh. Göttingen 13, 1867). The recipient is almost certainly the editor of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876, H. Weber, with Dedekind). The letter answers editorial queries keyed to page and line numbers of the printed memoir (S. 12, 16, 17 on the previous page). There is no derivation on this page, only editorial verdicts.

(1) On S. 17 Hattendorff made no change, because his text agrees with Riemann's manuscript ('M.-S.').

(2) He confirms that the auxiliary functions k_1 and k_2 become discontinuous (singular) only at 'the three factors'. This presumably means the three points t where the linear factors of phi(t)*chi(t) vanish (my interpretation). These are the branch points of the conformal parametrisation, in the setting where dv/dt = 1/sqrt(phi(t)*chi(t)), the equation the previous page proposes to keep.

(3) He considers it unnecessary to write down explicitly the linear second-order ODE satisfied by k. This would be a Fuchsian equation with three regular singular points, i.e. Riemann's P-function / hypergeometric type (my identification). His reason is that the first-order equation (c) of the memoir already reduces k to one of two other functions. The transcription renders these as '6' and '1'. In the hand they look like a Greek or Kurrent letter and a short letter, possibly sigma and s; this is uncertain.

(4) He encloses Riemann's manuscript and asks for it to be returned after use. The closing and signature follow.

Modern restatement of the only mathematical content: there is a multivalued function k(t), built from the minimal-surface parametrisation with dv/dt = (phi chi)^(-1/2). Its branches k_1, k_2 have singularities only at the three roots of phi*chi (or at three prescribed points). Because of this, k satisfies a second-order linear ODE with three regular singular points, solvable by hypergeometric functions. Hattendorff prefers to reduce k via a first-order relation (c) instead of exhibiting that ODE.
errors: No computation is present to check. The claim that k_1, k_2 are singular only at three points is asserted, not proved, on this page. It is consistent with Riemann's treatment of the minimal-surface examples via functions with three branch points.
The previous page records that Hattendorff had earlier made an error by not re-computing (1/k) d^2k/dv^2 at the points c. This page does not repeat that issue.

results.what: Editorial confirmation that the branches k_1, k_2 are singular only at three points, so k satisfies a second-order linear ODE with three singular points, reducible via a first-order equation (c)
results.modern_name: Riemann P-function / hypergeometric (Fuchsian) equation with three regular singular points, applied to Schwarz–Riemann minimal-surface constructions
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (P-functions 1857; minimal surface memoir published posthumously 1867, ed. Hattendorff)

results.what: Correspondence on the editing of Riemann's minimal-surface memoir for the Werke
results.modern_name: Editorial history of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an editorial letter by Hattendorff, not Riemann's mathematics. It only confirms known features of Riemann's published minimal-surface memoir (three singular points, reduction via a first-order equation). Its interest is purely philological: it documents the manuscript's circulation between editors.

checkable.asserts: Context only: the Gauss hypergeometric function solves the second-order ODE with three regular singular points 0, 1, oo. This is the type of equation Hattendorff says need not be written down explicitly.
The relation dv/dt = 1/sqrt(phi(t) chi(t)), carried over from the previous page. Its singular points are the zeros of phi*chi.

transcription_corrections: 'auf die Function 6' and 'auf die Function 1': the symbols are probably letters (e.g. sigma and s, or similar Kurrent letters) rather than the digits 6 and 1; the reading is uncertain.
'für die drei Factoren unstetig' matches the hand; the sense is probably the three (linear) factors, i.e. their zero points.
'M.-S.' is written 'M. S.' (Manuscript); 'Hülfe' and 'gefälligst' are confirmed.
